lesson.title: Design an AI-supported unit
lesson.subtitle: Learning first, AI where it helps

video.title: Design an AI-supported unit
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Dr Farah Rahman — teacher educator, Bangladesh (main character)
Mr Okafor — Grade 8 science teacher, Nigeria (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

chapters.label: The lab: a tree you can read

scenes.visual: A training room. A young teacher holds up a unit plan: twelve lesson boxes, each stamped with a different app tile. Dr Farah studies it, then taps the empty line at the top labelled ‘Learning goals’.
scenes.animation: App tiles pop onto the boxes one after another (fast, 100 ms each); Farah’s finger taps the empty line.
scenes.narration: A young teacher proudly showed me her unit plan: a new AI tool every lesson. I asked: what should the pupils learn?

scenes.visual: Paper-grey card. The Darsi mark pops in, then the course name, the lesson title and a yellow ‘AI’ track chip with the spark icon.
scenes.animation: Mark scales 0→100% with a small overshoot (≤ 200 ms); title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: design a unit where AI serves the learning.

scenes.visual: A flow builds left to right: a target (learning goals), a checked sheet (evidence), pupils working (activities), and last a small spark (AI where it helps).
scenes.animation: Nodes appear one by one with arrows drawing between them.
scenes.narration: Plan backwards. Start with the goals: what pupils should know and do by the end. Then the evidence: how you’ll know they got there. Then the activities. Only then ask where AI could help.

scenes.visual: Three trays on a teacher’s desk: ‘helps me’ (a draft with a teacher’s pen), ‘pupils use it’ (a level badge), ‘stays out’ (a closed tray with pupils thinking hard).
scenes.animation: Each tray slides in as it is said.
scenes.narration: For each activity, AI has three places. It can help you, drafting questions or simpler texts that you check. Pupils can use it, with a set AI level. Or it stays out, where the struggle is the learning.

scenes.visual: Two rules pinned to a board. Rule one: a printer page, a phone shared by a group of four, a teacher at the front. Rule two: a magnifying glass over an AI-made worksheet, ticking facts, level, bias and local fit.
scenes.animation: Each rule slides in; the magnifying glass sweeps the worksheet.
scenes.narration: Two rules for every plan. Each AI activity has a no-device path: a printout, one phone per group, or a demonstration. And everything AI makes is checked for facts, level, bias and local fit before pupils see it.

scenes.visual: Clean white card with the AI track chip. Four cards: planned from goals, AI where it helps, works for every pupil, a person checks.
scenes.animation: Cards appear one by one, 300 ms apart.
scenes.narration: So an AI-supported unit starts from goals, uses AI only where it helps, includes every pupil, and keeps a person checking. AI is a tool in the plan, not the plan.

scenes.visual: A home kitchen. A pressure cooker whistles over a pot of beans; beside it, someone chops a fresh salad by hand. A meal plan is pinned to the wall.
scenes.animation: The cooker’s whistle puffs; the knife chops in a short loop.
scenes.on_screen_text: Plan the meal, then the cooker
scenes.narration: It’s like a pressure cooker. It saves hours on beans, but nobody makes a salad in it. You plan the meal first, then use the cooker where it helps.

scenes.visual: Dr Farah pops in beside the three trays, pointing at the closed one. Three answer cards drop in below her.
scenes.animation: Character slides in from the side; answer cards drop in with a small bounce.
scenes.narration: Quick check! When should AI stay out of a lesson?

scenes.visual: The card ‘When the struggle is the learning’ gets a blue check badge. A pupil writes an argument by hand; another reads a rainfall bar graph with a finger; afterwards, a small chat bubble offers feedback.
scenes.animation: Check badge pops (150 ms); the feedback bubble arrives last.
scenes.on_screen_text: Where the struggle is the learning
scenes.narration: When the struggle is the learning. If the goal is writing an argument, pupils write it. If it’s reading a rainfall graph, they read it themselves. AI can come in afterwards, to give feedback.

scenes.visual: A three-week planner titled ‘Floods’. Week by week: a teacher checking AI-drafted worksheets at three levels; a group around one phone comparing tips with a printed leaflet; pupils reading a bottle rain gauge and interviewing an elder under a tree.
scenes.animation: Planner pages turn week by week.
scenes.narration: Here’s a three-week science unit on floods. AI drafts the teacher’s rainfall worksheets at three levels, and she checks them. Groups ask a chatbot on one phone for flood-safety tips and check them against the official leaflet. AI stays out of their rain-gauge readings and interviews with elders.

scenes.visual: Two quiz sheets, before and after, with the after scores higher; a stack of pupils’ work; speech bubbles of pupils’ views. Then a staff meeting: the teacher shares one slide while colleagues take notes.
scenes.animation: Score bars grow; the staff-meeting scene fades in.
scenes.narration: Then judge the unit. Give a short quiz before and after, look at pupils’ work, and ask their views. Share what worked, and what didn’t, at a staff meeting. That’s how a whole school learns.

scenes.visual: A phone screen with the Decision tree lab: a table of fourteen days (sky, temperature, humidity, wind, played outside), and a tree growing from ‘What is the sky like?’ into branches that end in ‘Play outside’ or ‘Stay inside’.
scenes.animation: The tree grows branch by branch (1.5 s); the matching days highlight in the table.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: a tree to read
scenes.narration: In the app, fourteen days of weather show when a class played football at break. Build a decision tree, one question at a time, or let the computer pick. You see exactly why it decides, so pupils can question it.

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor in his classroom, a register in hand: half the names have a small phone icon, half don’t. Two answer cards appear beside him.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Half my class has no phone at home. How should my unit use AI?

scenes.visual: The ‘AI work in class, in groups’ card gets the check badge, then the screen resolves into the four points of an AI-supported unit.
scenes.animation: Points tick in, 250 ms apart; the takeaway bar slides up.
scenes.on_screen_text: Goals first, AI where it helps
scenes.narration: AI work in class, in groups, with a paper path, so no pupil is left out. Remember: goals first, AI only where it helps, everything checked, and the unit judged and shared.

scenes.visual: A classroom. Pupils call out days and weather; the teacher tallies them in a table on the board, then draws a tree of yes-or-no questions beside it. A pupil points at one branch, asking where it might go wrong. Dr Farah smiles beside the board.
scenes.animation: Table rows appear; the tree draws itself branch by branch.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: a “Decision tree from our data”. The class lists the last ten school days: the weather, and whether they played outside. Together, build a tree of yes-or-no questions on the board. Then ask: where would our tree go wrong?

checkpoints.prompt: When should AI stay out of a lesson?

options.text: When the struggle is the learning

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — if the goal is to write an argument or read a graph, pupils must do that thinking themselves.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — AI doesn’t help every activity, and exams aren’t the only place. Keep it out where the struggle is the learning.

checkpoints.prompt: Half of Mr Okafor’s class has no phone at home. How should his unit use AI?

options.text: AI homework for pupils with phones
AI work in class, in groups

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — AI work in class, in groups, with a paper path, leaves no pupil out.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — AI homework only for pupils with phones leaves half the class behind. Do the AI parts in class, in groups.
